_README: Minimum Support Price, rupees per quintal, as announced by the Cabinet
on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and
Prices (CACP). MSP is a floor the government undertakes to buy at, not
a forecast and not the market rate -- the market often pays more, and
where procurement is thin a farmer may not be able to realise it.
These figures were checked against the Cabinet's own press releases on
the date in verified_on, release by release, and every number below
appears in the 'MSP 2026-27' column of the tables cited in verified_from.
RE-CHECK EACH SEASON. The Cabinet revises kharif MSP around May and
rabi around October, and a stale table is worse than none: the figures
that were here before this check were the 2025-26 column, a full season
out of date, and every one of the fourteen was wrong by between 10 and
622 rupees a quintal. Nothing else needs changing when they are updated
-- correct the numbers, the marketing_year, and verified_on.
Where the Cabinet announces two grades, the lower is carried here:
paddy common (2441) not Grade A (2461), jowar hybrid (4023) not
maldandi (4073), cotton medium staple (8267) not long staple (8667).
The crop keys in this platform do not distinguish those grades, and a
floor price quoted too high is the harmful direction of the error -- a
farmer who holds out for a number nobody will pay loses the season.
A crop absent from this file simply has no MSP shown. That is the
right behaviour for fruit, vegetables and anything outside the MSP
list, which is most of what many farmers actually grow. The mandated
list also covers crops this platform has no water-balance calibration
for -- ragi, tur, moong, urad, sesamum, nigerseed, lentil, safflower --
and those are left out rather than carried unusable.
source: CACP / Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
